scope: Full exact client and six component source files read, UTF8/SHA256/Git blob checked
Focused on exercise/run_case/joined_cancel_or_clean and the same receive_body used by the QA runtime
No independent repeat of h2 crate upstream EOS review
verified_boundaries: ResetZeroBeforeEos and EofBeforeEos send the two declared bytes with end_stream=false. Client consumes exactly those bytes, checks expected=2 and !is_end_stream, releases capacity, then sends the one consumption acknowledgement before the server injects reset or aborts the owned server driver.

Both negative tests require bytes=2, exact inner h2_data_error, response_complete=false and recv_end_stream=false. Data-EOS and empty-trailer-EOS positive controls require successful actual receive_body completion.

The runtime receive_body does not treat Content-Length satisfaction as EOS. It continues data until None, awaits trailers, rejects nonempty trailers or missing receive EOS, and requires exact body length before setting response_complete.

Client and server driver handles are actually awaited. A synthetic negative may accept only the explicitly allowed driver connection error; the receive result remains an error. Server operation error, unexpected request, join panic or component timeout fails run_case and cannot satisfy the positive tests.
The duplicate Content-Length assertion calls the real header parser with two values. The short-EOS case remains a deliberately broad rejection check, not an assertion of a specific transport error.
Original-deadline helper negatives call the actual conversion function. Components use a separate two-second local timeout; they do not claim to exercise a fifteen-second product request.
limitations: Source-only review; no Rust compile, component execution, actual socket, TLS, product, host, or credential access performed by this reviewer.
The in-memory components exercise the QA body receiver and h2 drivers, not the whole exchange TLS/pinning path. They do not establish product or official CLI qualification.

A complete body flag alone is insufficient for future runtime PASS. The caller must retain authoritative client exit zero, no error, actual driver joined, completion/publication within the original deadline, and its independent body semantics.
A timeout is a failed component result; this source review does not claim an explicit joined-task observation on every cancelled timeout path.
